1.note: If your language would not represent a number in a form such as **fourth**, you could represent this number in a form that your language would use. Alternate translation: [in year four]

Jeremiah is using the phrase translated as **The word that came to Jeremiah concerning all of the people of Judah** to introduce a new event in the story. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new event.

Jeremiah is using **The word that came to Jeremiah** as a common expression of the culture to mean “Yahweh spoke a message to Jeremiah.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [The message that Yahweh spoke to Jeremiah]

Here Jeremiah is providing background information to help readers understand what happens next in the story. In your translation, introduce this information in a way that would be natural in your own language and culture.

2.q: אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֜ר יִרְמְיָ֤הוּ הַ⁠נָּבִיא֙ עַל־כָּל־עַ֣ם יְהוּדָ֔ה וְ⁠אֶ֛ל כָּל־יֹשְׁבֵ֥י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם לֵ⁠אמֹֽר
2.note: The term **saying** introduces a direct quotation. In your translation, use a natural way of introducing direct quotations in your language. It may not be necessary to represent this term explicitly.

3.q: מִן־שְׁלֹ֣שׁ עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֡ה לְ⁠יֹאשִׁיָּ֣הוּ בֶן־אָמוֹן֩ מֶ֨לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֜ה וְ⁠עַ֣ד הַ⁠יּ֣וֹם הַ⁠זֶּ֗ה זֶ֚ה שָׁלֹ֤שׁ וְ⁠עֶשְׂרִים֙ שָׁנָ֔ה הָיָ֥ה דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה אֵלָ֑⁠י וָ⁠אֲדַבֵּ֧ר אֲלֵי⁠כֶ֛ם אַשְׁכֵּ֥ים וְ⁠דַבֵּ֖ר וְ⁠לֹ֥א שְׁמַעְתֶּֽם
3.note: The events that Jeremiah describes here did not all happen at one time. They took place over the **twenty-three years** from **the thirteenth year of Josiah** until the day on which he was speaking. Your language may have a connecting phrase that you can use to show this. Alternate translation: [Again and again, from the year thirteen of Josiah son of Amon, king of Judah, until this very day—a period of twenty-three years—the word of Yahweh has kept coming to me, and time after time I have spoken to you, but you have never listened]
The word **Amon** is the name of a man, a king of Judah.

Here Jeremiah is providing background information to help readers understand what happens next in the story. In your translation, introduce this information in a way that would be natural in your own language and culture.
See how you translated the similar expression in 8:9.
See how you translated **rising early and speaking** in 7:13.

4.note: The pronoun **you** refers to the people of Judah, together with their ancestors who lived in earlier generations. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And Yahweh has sent to you people of Judah and to your ancestors, all of his servants the prophets]

Jeremiah is using **rising early and sending** as a common expression of the culture to mean “sending them again and again.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [sending them repeatedly]
See how you translated the similar expression in 7:24.

Jeremiah is using **you have not extended your ear to hear** as a common expression of the culture to mean “you have not been willing to pay attention.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and you have not been willing to pay attention]

5.note: The term **saying** introduces a direct quotation. In your translation, use a natural way of introducing direct quotations in your language. It may not be necessary to represent this term explicitly.

The word translated as **and** indicates that what follows is a result of what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a result of what came before. Alternate translation: [and then you will dwell on the land] or [so that you may dwell on the land]

Here the masculine term **man** has a generic sense that includes both men and women. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use language in your translation that is clearly inclusive of both men and women. Alternate translation: [each person from his or her evil way]

Jeremiah is speaking of how a person lives as if that were a **way** or path that the person was walking along. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [from his evil behavior]

Yahweh is speaking of himself in the third person as **that Yahweh gave to you** and later as **provoke me to anger** shifting to first person, but here specifically as the phrase implied by the surrounding third-person reference to himself. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the first person. Alternate translation: [and from the evil of your deeds against me]

Jeremiah is using **from everlasting to everlasting** as a common expression of the culture to mean “forever.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [for all time] or [forever]

6.q: וְ⁠אַל־תֵּלְכ֗וּ אַֽחֲרֵי֙ אֱלֹהִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֔ים לְ⁠עָבְדָ֖⁠ם וּ⁠לְ⁠הִשְׁתַּחֲוֺ֣ת לָ⁠הֶ֑ם
6.note: Here, **to** marks **to serve them and to bow down to them** as the goal or purpose of going **after other gods**. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that this is the purpose. Alternate translation: [And do not follow the way of other gods in order to serve them and worship them]

To **bow down to** idols was a symbolic action by which the people of Judah showed submission and worship to those false gods. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action in the text of your translation or in a footnote. Alternate translation: [and to prostrate yourselves before them]
See how you translated the similar expression in 1:16. This also occurs in verses 7 and 14. Alternate translation: [with gods you yourself have crafted]

7.q: וְ⁠לֹֽא & לְמַ֧עַן הכעסו⁠ני בְּ⁠מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה יְדֵי⁠כֶ֖ם לְ⁠רַ֥ע לָ⁠כֶֽם
7.note: The phrase translated as **so as to** indicates that what follows is a result of what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a result of what came before. Alternate translation: [and as a result you have provoked me to anger with the work of your hands, so that harm has come to you]
See how you translated **the declaration of Yahweh** in 1:8. This also occurs in verses 9, 12, 29, and 31.

8.note: The term translated as **Therefore** indicates that what follows is a result of what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes this clear. Alternate translation: [This is why]

This is the beginning of what Yahweh said. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could mark that this is a direct quote of Yahweh. See how you translated the similar expression in 2:5. This also occurs in verses 15, 27, 28, and 32 of this chapter.
See how you translated this name in 19:11.

The word translated as **Because** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [Since]

9.note: Yahweh is using **behold me sending** as a common expression of the culture to mean that he was about to do something. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Now I am about to send]

If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **a horror** and **a hissing** and **an eternal desolation**, you could express the same ideas in another way. Alternate translation: [something horrifying that people will hiss at and it will be desolate forever]

The terms **a horror** and **a hissing** and **an eternal desolation** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the three terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [a permanent ruin that appalls everyone who sees it]

Here, **a hissing** represents the scorn that people will express toward these ruined places. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. This also occurs in verse 18. Alternate translation: [and an object of scorn]
See how you translated the similar expression in 19:8. This also occurs in verse 18.

10.q: ק֤וֹל שָׂשׂוֹן֙ וְ⁠ק֣וֹל שִׂמְחָ֔ה ק֥וֹל חָתָ֖ן וְ⁠ק֣וֹל כַּלָּ֑ה ק֥וֹל רֵחַ֖יִם וְ⁠א֥וֹר נֵֽר
10.note: Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe the **sound** and the **light** that each of these things produces. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the joyful sounds and the glad sounds, the sounds that a bridegroom and a bride make, the sounds that millstones make and the light that a lamp shines]
See how you translated this expression in 7:34. This also occurs in verse 10.
See how you translated the similar expression in 7:34.

Here, **the sound of the millstones and the light of the lamp** represents the ordinary daily activity of household life. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [all the everyday activity of their households]

11.note: If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **a ruin** and **a desolation**, you could express the same ideas in another way. Alternate translation: [ruined and deserted]

The terms **a ruin** and **a desolation** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [a completely desolate ruin]

12.q: וְ⁠הָיָ֣ה כִ⁠מְלֹ֣אות שִׁבְעִ֣ים שָׁנָ֡ה אֶפְקֹ֣ד עַל־מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶל֩ וְ⁠עַל־הַ⁠גּ֨וֹי הַ⁠ה֧וּא נְאֻם־יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־עֲוֺנָ֖⁠ם וְ⁠עַל־אֶ֣רֶץ כַּשְׂדִּ֑ים וְ⁠שַׂמְתִּ֥י אֹת֖⁠וֹ לְ⁠שִֽׁמְמ֥וֹת עוֹלָֽם
12.note: The events that Yahweh describes here will not happen right away. They will happen only after the **seventy years** of exile to Babylon are complete. Your language may have a connecting phrase that you can use to show this. Alternate translation: [But only after those seventy years have come to an end will I punish the king of Babylon and that nation”—the declaration of Yahweh—“for their iniquity, and the land of the Chaldeans, and then I will make it a perpetual desolation]

The expression **are fulfilled** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [when seventy years come to an end]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **iniquity**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [because they acted wickedly]
The word **Chaldeans** is the name of a people group which settled in Babylon. It came to mean the same as “Babylonians.”

13.note: The phrase **that land** refers to the land of the Chaldeans, which Yahweh spoke about in the previous verse. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [the land of the Chaldeans] or [Babylon]

The expression **is written** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [all of that which this book records]

The pronoun **I** refers to Yahweh, who is speaking, while **Jeremiah** is spoken about by name. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [which I, Yahweh, caused my prophet Jeremiah to prophesy against all of the nations]

14.note: The word translated as **For** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [This is because]

The phrase **will also make them serve, even them** refers to the Babylonians, whom Yahweh has been speaking about. He repeats the word “them” for emphasis. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [will also make those Babylonians serve their nations]

The expressions **according to their deed** and **according to the work of their hands** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two expressions together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [according to everything they have done]

15.q: כִּ֣י כֹה֩ אָמַ֨ר יְהוָ֜ה אֱלֹהֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֵלַ֔⁠י
15.note: This is the beginning of what Yahweh said to Jeremiah. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could mark that this is a direct quote of Yahweh.
See how you translated the similar expression in 21:4.

Here Yahweh is speaking of the judgment that he will bring on the nations as if it were **this cup of the wine of the wrath** that they must drink. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [this cup, which represents my angry judgment]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe **wine** that is characterized by **the wrath**, that is, wine that represents his anger. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [this cup of wine that represents my wrath]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **wrath**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [what I do because I am angry]

Here, **my hand** represents Yahweh’s power and authority. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [from my authority]
See how you translated the similar expression in 21:4.

16.note: Here Yahweh is speaking of the nations suffering his judgment as if they would **drink** and **stagger** and **act like madmen** from too much wine. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And they will be overwhelmed and will stumble about and will lose their senses]

Yahweh is using **from the face of** as a common expression of the culture to mean “because of.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [because of the sword]

Yahweh is speaking of **the sword** as if it were a living thing that could be sent somewhere. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. This also occurs in verse 27. Alternate translation: [the armies that I am sending to attack them with swords]

17.q: וָ⁠אֶקַּ֥ח אֶת־הַ⁠כּ֖וֹס מִ⁠יַּ֣ד יְהוָ֑ה וָֽ⁠אַשְׁקֶה֙ אֶת־כָּל־הַ⁠גּוֹיִ֔ם אֲשֶׁר־שְׁלָחַ֥⁠נִי יְהוָ֖ה אֲלֵי⁠הֶֽם
17.note: These two actions did not happen at the same time. Jeremiah first **took the cup from the hand of Yahweh** and then **made all of the nations drink**. Your language may have a connecting phrase that you can use to show this. Alternate translation: [So I took the cup from the hand of Yahweh, and as time went on, I made all of the nations drink, those to which Yahweh had sent me]

17.q: וָ⁠אֶקַּ֥ח אֶת־הַ⁠כּ֖וֹס מִ⁠יַּ֣ד יְהוָ֑ה וָֽ⁠אַשְׁקֶה֙ אֶת־כָּל־הַ⁠גּוֹיִ֔ם
17.note: Here Jeremiah is speaking of announcing Yahweh’s judgment to the nations as if he **took the cup from the hand of Yahweh** and **made all of the nations drink** from it. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And I received Yahweh’s message of judgment from him, and I announced that judgment to all of the nations]

18.note: Here, **to** marks **to make them a ruin, a desolation, a hissing, and a curse** as the goal or purpose of making these people drink from the cup. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that this is the purpose. Alternate translation: [so that they would be a ruin]
The pronoun **its** refers to Judah rather than to Jerusalem. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [and the kings of Judah and the officials of Judah]

If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **a ruin** and **a desolation** and **a hissing** and **a curse**, you could express the same ideas in another way. Alternate translation: [ruined and deserted, so that people hiss at them and curse them]

The terms **a ruin** and **a desolation** and **a hissing** and **a curse** mean similar things. Jeremiah is using the terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [a complete wasteland]

19.note: Jeremiah is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [I also made Pharaoh, king of Egypt, and his servants and his officials and all of his people drink it]

20.q: וְ⁠אֵת֙ כָּל־הָ⁠עֶ֔רֶב וְ⁠אֵ֕ת כָּל־מַלְכֵ֖י אֶ֣רֶץ הָ⁠ע֑וּץ
20.note: Jeremiah is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and I gave the cup to all of the mixed people, and to all of the kings of the land of Uz]

21.note: Jeremiah is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and I gave the cup to the kings of Edom and the kings of Moab and the kings of the sons of Ammon]
Jeremiah is speaking as if the people of Ammon were actually the **sons** of their ancestor Ammon. Alternate translation: [and the Ammonites]

23.note: The expression **the ones cut at the corner of their hair** describes people who trimmed the hair at the sides of their heads as part of the worship of their gods. If your readers would not be familiar with this practice, you could use the name of a similar practice that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [and those who trim the hair at the sides of their heads]

The expression **the ones cut at the corner of their hair** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [all of those who cut off the corner of their hair]

26.note: Jeremiah is using the adjectives **the near** and **the far** as nouns to mean certain kinds of kingdoms. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate these adjectives with equivalent phrases. Alternate translation: [the kings who are near and the kings who are far away]

Jeremiah is referring to all of the kings of the north by naming two major components, **the near** and **the far**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [wherever they live] or [whether near or far away]

Jeremiah is using **a man to his brother** as a common expression of the culture to mean “one after another.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [each one in turn]

Here the masculine terms **a man** and **his brother** have a generic sense that includes both men and women. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use language in your translation that is clearly inclusive of both men and women. Alternate translation: [one person to another]

Jeremiah is using **on the face of the earth** as a common expression of the culture to mean “on the surface of the earth.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. This also occurs in verse 33. Alternate translation: [are on the surface of the earth]

**Sheshach** is a code name for Babylon. The code is based on substituting the last letter of the Hebrew alphabet for the first letter, the next to last letter for the next to first letter, etc. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers, or put the information in a footnote. Alternate translation: [And the king of Sheshach, that is, the king of Babylon,] or [And the king of Babylon]
See how you translated the similar expression in 24:9.

27.q: וְ⁠אָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵי⁠הֶ֡ם כֹּֽה־אָמַר֩ יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל
27.note: Yahweh is using the phrase **Thus says Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel** to indicate that what follows is a direct quotation from Yahweh and comes with Yahweh’s authority. In your translation, use a natural way of indicating direct quotations in your language.

27.q: וְ⁠אָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵי⁠הֶ֡ם כֹּֽה־אָמַר֩ יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל שְׁת֤וּ
27.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [Then you shall tell them that Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, says: Drink]

27.q: שְׁת֤וּ וְ⁠שִׁכְרוּ֙ וּ⁠קְי֔וּ וְ⁠נִפְל֖וּ וְ⁠לֹ֣א תָק֑וּמוּ
27.note: Here Yahweh is speaking of the judgment that the nations will suffer as if it were wine that would make them **be drunk** and **vomit** and **fall**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Suffer my judgment and stagger and be sickened and be ruined, and never recover]
The pronoun **you** refers to Jeremiah. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [Then you, Jeremiah, shall say to those kingdoms which I will punish]

27.q: מִ⁠פְּנֵ֣י הַ⁠חֶ֔רֶב אֲשֶׁ֛ר אָנֹכִ֥י שֹׁלֵ֖חַ בֵּינֵי⁠כֶֽם
27.note: Yahweh is using **from the face of** as a common expression of the culture to mean “because of.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. This also occurs in verse 16. Alternate translation: [because of the sword that I am sending among you]

Yahweh is speaking of **the sword** as if it were a living thing that could be sent among people. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the war that I am causing to come upon you]

28.q: וְ⁠הָיָ֗ה כִּ֧י יְמָאֲנ֛וּ לָ⁠קַֽחַת־הַ⁠כּ֥וֹס מִ⁠יָּדְ⁠ךָ֖ לִ⁠שְׁתּ֑וֹת
28.note: Yahweh is presenting a possible condition, that the nations might **refuse to take the cup** that Jeremiah offers them. Use a natural form in your language for introducing a condition that could happen. It may be helpful to reorder this sentence so that the conditional statement is first. Alternate translation: [If they refuse to take the cup from your hand to drink]

Yahweh is using a construction in which a verb and its object come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [You must drink it!]

29.note: Yahweh is using the term **behold** to focus his listeners’ attention on what he is about to say. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [See!]

The expression **is called** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [in the city over which people call my name]

Yahweh is using **the city over which my name is called** as a common expression of the culture to mean “the city that belongs to me.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [in the city that belongs to me]

The pronoun **you** refers to the nations that Yahweh is addressing, not to the city that he has just spoken about. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [and you nations]

The expressions **being acquitted** and **will you be acquitted** and **You will not be acquitted** are passive verbal forms. If it would be unnatural to use those forms, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [will I surely acquit you? I will not acquit you]

Yahweh is using the question form to emphasize that the nations will certainly not escape punishment. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [you will certainly not go unpunished! You will surely be punished]

29.q: כִּ֣י & חֶ֗רֶב אֲנִ֤י קֹרֵא֙ עַל־כָּל־יֹשְׁבֵ֣י הָ⁠אָ֔רֶץ
29.note: Yahweh is using **a sword** to represent war or violent death. Alternate translation: [I am causing there to be war against all of the inhabitants of the earth]

30.note: Yahweh is stating the pronoun **you** separately, even though the verb translated as **you will prophesy** already includes this meaning. He is doing that to emphasize that he is speaking directly to Jeremiah, giving him this command. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation.
